key_insight: Flide targets fast categorical decisions rather than text generation. Its core idea is exact state forking: reuse computation across decision branches without distorting output probabilities.
problem_solved: Generation-oriented inference engines poorly serve decision models such as Jev, either repeatedly computing shared prefixes or producing distorted probabilities.
method: Build an inference engine specifically for categorical decision workloads.
Use exact state forking to reuse shared-prefix computation across alternative decision branches.
Preserve output probabilities while reducing redundant inference work.
impact: Flide aims to make lightweight, rapid reasoning more efficient for LLM agents without sacrificing probability fidelity. The supplied abstract is incomplete and provides no quantitative performance results.
visual_elements: Decision tree showing a shared prefix splitting into alternative branches.
Side-by-side execution diagrams: repeated prefix computation versus shared state with forks.
Probability bars illustrating exact preservation versus distorted outputs.
LLM-agent workflow highlighting a fast categorical decision stage.
paper_title: Flide: Accelerating Decision Inference with Exact State Forking
paper_authors: Bobo Li, Jiajia Song, Hao Fei, Wynne Hsu, Mong Li Lee
